topics.label: SOLID Principles
topics.desc: Five OO design heuristics (SRP, OCP, LSP, ISP, DIP) for building maintainable, loosely coupled class structures that absorb change.

topics.label: DRY
topics.desc: Don't Repeat Yourself: each piece of knowledge has one authoritative representation, eliminating divergence from duplicated logic.

topics.label: KISS & YAGNI
topics.desc: Favor the simplest design that works and avoid speculative features until actually needed, curbing accidental complexity.

topics.label: Separation of Concerns
topics.desc: Partition a system so each part addresses one concern, limiting the knowledge any module needs and easing reasoning.

topics.label: Coupling & Cohesion
topics.desc: The twin metrics of good structure: minimize inter-module dependencies while maximizing relatedness within a module.

topics.label: Composition Over Inheritance
topics.desc: Prefer assembling behavior from objects over deep class hierarchies, avoiding fragile base classes and rigid taxonomies.

topics.label: Information Hiding
topics.desc: Encapsulate volatile design decisions behind stable interfaces so internal changes don't ripple across clients.

topics.label: GoF Pattern Catalog
topics.desc: The canonical 23 reusable solutions classified as creational, structural, and behavioral, giving shared design vocabulary.

topics.label: Creational Patterns
topics.desc: Factory, Builder, Singleton, Prototype, and Abstract Factory decouple object construction from the code that uses objects.

topics.label: Structural Patterns
topics.desc: Adapter, Decorator, Facade, Proxy, and Composite compose objects into larger structures while keeping them flexible.

topics.label: Behavioral Patterns
topics.desc: Strategy, Observer, Command, State, and Visitor define how objects collaborate and distribute responsibility at runtime.

topics.label: Dependency Injection
topics.desc: Supply collaborators externally rather than constructing them internally, enabling substitution, testing, and inversion of control.

topics.label: Inversion of Control
topics.desc: Hand control of flow and object lifecycle to a framework or container, the principle underlying DI and plugin systems.

topics.label: Repository Pattern
topics.desc: Mediate between domain and data layers with a collection-like abstraction, isolating persistence concerns from business logic.

topics.label: Anti-Patterns
topics.desc: Recurring bad solutions—God Object, Big Ball of Mud, Spaghetti Code—whose recognition steers teams toward better structure.

topics.label: Layered Architecture
topics.desc: Stack responsibilities into presentation, business, and data tiers with downward dependencies, the default enterprise organization.

topics.label: Hexagonal Architecture
topics.desc: Ports-and-adapters style isolating domain logic from I/O so external technologies plug in without touching the core.

topics.label: Clean Architecture
topics.desc: Concentric layers with the dependency rule pointing inward toward stable business rules, keeping frameworks at the edge.

topics.label: Event-Driven Architecture
topics.desc: Components communicate via asynchronous events, decoupling producers from consumers for scalability and loose coupling.

topics.label: Monolith vs Distributed
topics.desc: The foundational trade-off between deploying as one unit versus many services, weighing simplicity against independent scaling.

topics.label: CQRS & Event Sourcing
topics.desc: Separate read and write models, optionally persisting state as an append-only event log for auditability and replay.

topics.label: Microkernel & Plugins
topics.desc: A minimal core plus pluggable feature modules, enabling extensibility and product-line variation without core changes.

topics.label: Ubiquitous Language
topics.desc: A shared, rigorous vocabulary between domain experts and code that keeps the model and its implementation aligned.

topics.label: Bounded Context
topics.desc: An explicit boundary within which a model and its language are consistent, preventing concepts from leaking and colliding.

topics.label: Aggregates & Roots
topics.desc: Clusters of entities and value objects treated as one consistency boundary, mutated only through a single aggregate root.

topics.label: Entities & Value Objects
topics.desc: Distinguish objects defined by identity over time from immutable objects defined wholly by their attribute values.

topics.label: Domain Services & Events
topics.desc: Model stateless domain operations and significant occurrences that don't belong to any single entity or value object.

topics.label: Context Mapping
topics.desc: Document relationships between bounded contexts—shared kernel, anti-corruption layer, conformist—to manage team integration.

topics.label: Strategic Design
topics.desc: Identify core, supporting, and generic subdomains to focus design effort and investment where competitive value lives.

topics.label: API Contracts
topics.desc: Formal agreements on requests, responses, and errors that let producers and consumers evolve independently and reliably.

topics.label: Resource-Oriented Design
topics.desc: Model APIs around resources, uniform verbs, and statelessness so clients interact predictably through standard semantics.

topics.label: API Versioning
topics.desc: Strategies—URI, header, media-type—for evolving an interface without breaking existing consumers depending on it.

topics.label: Backward Compatibility
topics.desc: Disciplines for changing schemas and behavior additively so older clients keep working as the contract grows.

topics.label: Idempotency & Safety
topics.desc: Designing operations so retries produce no extra effect, essential for reliability over unreliable networks.

topics.label: Interface Design
topics.desc: Craft minimal, hard-to-misuse abstractions where the easy path is the correct one and intent is self-documenting.

topics.label: Error & Pagination Design
topics.desc: Consistent error envelopes, status codes, and pagination conventions that make an API robust and predictable to integrate.

topics.label: Modularization
topics.desc: Decompose a system into independently comprehensible units with explicit interfaces, the primary tool against complexity.

topics.label: Encapsulation
topics.desc: Bundle state with the operations on it and restrict access, protecting invariants and enabling local reasoning.

topics.label: Dependency Management
topics.desc: Control the direction and weight of dependencies between modules to keep the dependency graph acyclic and stable.

topics.label: Acyclic Dependencies
topics.desc: Forbid cycles among components so each can be built, tested, and released without dragging the whole graph along.

topics.label: Component Cohesion
topics.desc: Principles (REP, CCP, CRP) for deciding which classes belong together in a releasable, reusable component.

topics.label: Package & Module Boundaries
topics.desc: Organize code into packages whose boundaries express architecture and enforce visibility, not just file convenience.

topics.label: Extensibility Points
topics.desc: Designed seams—hooks, SPIs, plugins—that let a system grow capability without modifying its existing core code.

topics.label: Quality Attributes
topics.desc: The non-functional requirements—performance, security, modifiability—that architecture exists primarily to satisfy.

topics.label: Maintainability
topics.desc: The ease of understanding, changing, and extending a system, the dominant lifetime cost driver of most software.

topics.label: Scalability
topics.desc: Designing so capacity grows with load via horizontal or vertical means without disproportionate cost or rework.

topics.label: Testability
topics.desc: Structuring code so behavior is easy to isolate, observe, and control, directly shaped by coupling and dependency choices.

topics.label: Architectural Trade-offs
topics.desc: Methods like ATAM for reasoning about how decisions help one quality attribute at the expense of another.

topics.label: Conway's Law
topics.desc: Systems mirror the communication structures of the organizations that build them, a force to design with deliberately.

topics.label: Refactoring
topics.desc: Disciplined, behavior-preserving code transformation to improve internal structure, ideally backed by tests.

topics.label: Code Smells
topics.desc: Surface symptoms—long methods, feature envy, shotgun surgery—that hint at deeper structural problems needing attention.

topics.label: Technical Debt
topics.desc: The accumulated cost of expedient design choices, which accrues interest as future change becomes slower and riskier.

topics.label: Strangler Fig Pattern
topics.desc: Incrementally replace a legacy system by routing functionality to new code until the old system can be retired.

topics.label: Legacy Modernization
topics.desc: Tactics—characterization tests, seams, branch by abstraction—for safely changing untested, entangled inherited code.

topics.label: Evolutionary Architecture
topics.desc: Treat architecture as something guided through incremental, reversible change rather than fixed up front.
